title: Lost money to a UPI or online fraud
triggers: money debited after I clicked a link
someone pretending to be from the bank took my OTP

rights.plain_explanation: Cheating someone by pretending to be someone else using a phone or computer is a crime (up to 3 years and a fine).
Fraudulently using someone's password, electronic signature or other unique identity feature is identity theft (up to 3 years and a fine).
Cheating someone into handing over money or property is a crime, punishable with up to seven years.

rights.act: RBI circular on customer liability (6 July 2017)
rights.plain_explanation: If you tell your bank within three working days about an unauthorised electronic transaction caused by a third-party breach, your liability is zero. The bank must credit the amount within 10 working days of your report and resolve the case within 90 days.

do_now: Call 1930 right away; quick reports can freeze the money.
Call your bank to block your card or UPI and report the transaction.
Report it on cybercrime.gov.in and note the complaint number.
Keep screenshots of messages, numbers and transaction IDs. Never share an OTP or PIN.
user_at_fault_cases: If you shared your OTP or PIN yourself, the bank may hold you partly liable. Still report it at once.

escalation.label: National Cybercrime Reporting Portal
escalation.detail: File the complaint and track it.

escalation.label: Bank, then RBI Ombudsman
escalation.detail: If the bank doesn't resolve it, escalate to the RBI Ombudsman.

escalation.label: Free legal aid
escalation.detail: Call NALSA on 15100 or visit your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at the district court. Women, children, people in custody and people below the income limit get a free lawyer.
